observed_original_abi.calling_convention: __thiscall (one register argument in ECX, read before any definite write and dereferenced; zero ordinary stack arguments; the callee pops nothing because 0x00c70e14 is the bare byte 0xc3, so the caller owns stack cleanup)
observed_original_abi.calling_convention_discrimination: THE BYTES DO NOT DISCRIMINATE __thiscall FROM __fastcall, and this record says so rather than pretending otherwise. What the listing PROVES and discriminates: exactly one register argument, arriving in ECX (0x00c70e00 reads ECX on entry as the base of the body's only memory operand); exactly zero ordinary stack arguments (no instruction in the body names a memory operand relative to ESP); zero bytes of callee cleanup, owned by the caller. The first of those REFUTES __cdecl, under which the receiver would arrive at [ESP+4] and the register-relative read at 0x00c70e00 would have no receiver to read through. What the listing CANNOT discriminate: for a function with one register argument and zero stack arguments the __thiscall and __fastcall forms emit IDENTICAL machine code, and no byte of this body distinguishes them - the derived record says so in its own candidate_conventions list ['__thiscall', '__fastcall']. What would distinguish them is a source-level fact the evidence does not carry: that the register argument is a C++ `this` on a class rather than an ordinary first parameter. Nothing in the pack names a class (class_type null, namespace null, sdk_type null, sdk_name null, receiver.bounds_only true), so that distinction is UNKNOWN. The __thiscall spelling above is therefore the derived ABI record's own name for the shape, adopted in preference to the Ghidra decompilation's __fastcall rendering - and that rendering is not independent evidence, because the live ghidra_function record for this VA carries ghidra_has_calling_convention: false, ghidra_calling_convention: null and ghidra_calling_convention_signal: 'no_information', with the role marked 'cross-validation-only'. The derived record's own confidence on its C7 conclusion is INFERRED with corroboration: not_available, and its cross_validation block reports agreement: false (ghidra no_information, persisted no_information). Nothing in this reconstruction depends on the difference: both candidates give the same code, the same one-ECX-argument shape and the same zero-byte cleanup.
observed_original_abi.receiver: ECX, read at 0x00c70e00 as the base of the body's only memory operand `dword ptr [ECX + 0x13c]` and never written before that read
observed_original_abi.return_note: unsigned at the source level: the tail path copies bits and the only immediate write is an unsigned 32-bit constant. Any ordered reading of the result belongs to the callers, not to this body.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: on the null arm the immediate 1 written by `MOV EAX,imm32` at 0x00c70e0f; on the non-null arm the 32-bit word the tail target reads at receiver+0x194
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: BOTH PATHS WRITE A FULL DWORD, and nothing wider or narrower is claimed. The null arm is `b8 01 00 00 00`, which is MOV EAX,imm32 - a 32-bit immediate write, not the 8-bit `MOV AL` form, so all thirty-two bits of EAX are written and the top three bytes are not left unproven. The non-null arm is a transfer to 0x00b8dab0, whose live body is `8b 81 94 01 00 00 c3` = `MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + 0x194]` / `RET`, a 32-bit load into the full register. What is NOT claimed: any source-level type (the derived record's return.type is null), any signedness (the body copies bits; the ordered reading belongs to the callers), and that the two paths' values are the same quantity - nothing in the evidence says they are, and the four sampled callers only order the result against 0x4 or 0x5, which is consistent with either.
observed_original_abi.locals: none; the body allocates no frame, saves no register and builds no record (derived parse record: frame.push_ebp false, frame.mov_ebp_esp false, frame.sub null, local_extent 0)
observed_original_abi.outgoing_calls: one, and it is a TAIL TRANSFER rather than a nested call: 0x00c70e0a `e9 a1 cc f1 ff` = JMP 0x00b8dab0 with no preceding frame teardown (derived record: tail_call.present true, form epilogue_then_jmp, after_frame_setup false)

observed_mechanics: 0x00c70e00 8b 89 3c 01 00 00 - MOV ECX,dword ptr [ECX + 0x13c]: ModRM 0x89 is mod=10 (a disp32 follows), reg=001 (ECX), rm=001 (ECX); the disp32 is 0x0000013c. Base and destination being the same register is the in-place load the whole chain-of-ECX argument depends on.
0x00c70e06 85 c9 - TEST ECX,ECX: ModRM 0xc9 is reg=001 (ECX) and rm=001 (ECX), so the FLAGS come from the LOADED WORD and not from the incoming receiver. The instruction writes EFLAGS only.
0x00c70e08 74 05 - JZ 0x00c70e0f: rel8 = 5, which is exactly the length of the instruction it skips, so the false arm lands on 0x00c70e0f and the TRUE arm is the whole tail transfer at 0x00c70e0a.

0x00c70e0a e9 a1 cc f1 ff - JMP 0x00b8dab0: rel32 = 0xfff1cca1, sign-extended to -930655, and 0x00c70e0a + 5 - 930655 = 0x00b8dab0 exactly. ECX is NOT REWRITTEN between 0x00c70e00 and this jump (TEST and JZ write EFLAGS only, and no frame teardown is needed because no frame was built), so the target receives the loaded word as its own ECX receiver.
0x00c70e0f b8 01 00 00 00 - MOV EAX,0x1: opcode b8+r is a 32-bit immediate write; the alternative 8-bit form b0+r would leave the top of EAX unproven and does not occur.
0x00c70e14 c3 - RET: single byte, no imm16; the callee pops nothing, so stack cleanup is 0 bytes and is owned by the caller.

Raw bytes at 0x00c70e00..0x00c70e17, read live from the program database: 8b 89 3c 01 00 00 85 c9 74 05 e9 a1 cc f1 ff b8 01 00 00 00 c3 cc cc cc. The body is 21 bytes (0x00c70e00..0x00c70e14, matching the live ghidra_function record's body_span_bytes 21 and body_end 00c70e14) and the three 0xcc bytes at 0x00c70e15..0x00c70e17 are alignment padding, NOT part of the body.

0x00b8dab0 8b 81 94 01 00 00 c3 cc - read live for this package: MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + 0x194] / RET, then INT3 pad. This is what makes the transfer's shape a byte-level fact rather than a name-level assumption, and it is why the promoted sibling package pkg-00b8dab0-field194-getter fits the target.

The committed xref export knowledgegraph/triage/xrefs-2540f2ca.tsv, read whole for this VA: 41 direct-call edges INTO 0x00c70e00 from 32 distinct caller functions, and exactly ONE edge out - `00c70e00 00b8dab0 direct-call 00c70e0a` - whose callsite_va is the JMP. The export records a tail transfer as a direct-call edge, so the one callee has an independent machine oracle.

semantic_findings: The entry is a receiver-field presence test whose answer is a 32-bit dword: load a pointer out of the receiver at +0x13c, and if it is non-null BECOME 0x00b8dab0 - hand that pointer over as a receiver and let it produce the answer - otherwise return the constant 1.

THE CHAIN OF ECX is the load-bearing fact and it is proved from the listing, not assumed: 0x00c70e00 reads ECX and overwrites it with the loaded word in the same instruction (ModRM 0x89, reg=ECX and rm=ECX); nothing between there and the JMP writes a register except EFLAGS; and 0x00b8dab0 reads through ECX (its ModRM 0x81 has rm=001). The value crossing the transfer is therefore the word at incoming-receiver + 0x13c.
The JZ's rel8 is 5, which is the length of the JMP it skips, so the two arms are exactly {transfer to 0x00b8dab0} and {return 1}. There is no third path and no fallthrough into the JMP.

The transfer is a TAIL call, not a nested call: there is no frame teardown to perform because no frame was built, and the callee's result lands in the same register the caller would have used. The derived record classifies the same body as `form: epilogue_then_jmp`, `after_frame_setup: false`.
41 direct-call edges in from 32 distinct callers, and exactly one out. Fan-in says nothing about the field's meaning and is not used as evidence for one.

The four sampled call sites (0x00ba0245, 0x00be2127, 0x00d56c57, 0x00ff749b) all put the receiver in ECX immediately before the call and push nothing between that write and the call - four of four, which is the observational counterpart of the zero-stack-argument claim. All four then order the result against a small constant (0x4 or 0x5) and none dereferences it.
Nothing is written. The whole body is a read, a test, a transfer and a constant, and the model test asserts the entire 0x688-byte fixture arena is byte-identical across every call.

tooling_findings.finding: NO TAIL-TRANSFER BODY CAN REACH A STATIC PASS, so none can be promoted. The derived ABI record for 0x00c70e00 carries `verdict: ABI_UNKNOWN` and the validator's ABI arm tests that verdict BEFORE the arm that would pass a source which declares the convention: the order is (FAIL on conflict) -> (FAIL on source/machine convention mismatch) -> (WARN when verdict == ABI_UNKNOWN) -> (WARN on low confidence) -> (PASS when the convention is present in the source span and in canonical metadata). With verdict ABI_UNKNOWN the PASS arm is unreachable, so the ABI check is WARN whatever a reconstruction writes - and the aggregate ladder gives PASS only when all eight structural checks PASS.
tooling_findings.evidence: Measured over every committed evidence pack: 7 of 651 packs carry `tail_call.present == true` (0x0102adf0, 0x00b5b820, 0x007c4000, 0x00c70e00, 0x00d1e610, 0x00e36650, 0x00980330) and ALL SEVEN carry `verdict: ABI_UNKNOWN` - 7 of 7, no exceptions. The inference record's own T2 entry gives the reason, at `confidence: UNKNOWN`: 'the function can reach a caller by transferring out of the listing, so the path that actually returns was never observed'.
tooling_findings.why_it_looks_wrong_for_this_body: The observation T2 rests on is incomplete here, and this body makes it obvious. 0x00c70e0f/0x00c70e14 IS a returning path in the same listing, the JZ that guards the transfer is a two-byte instruction whose rel8 is the length of the transfer, and the transfer's own target is a seven-instruction body (8b 81 94 01 00 00 c3) whose MOV EAX/RET was read live for this package. The path that actually returns was observed.
tooling_findings.secondary_symptom: The same record carries `abstained_because: []`, so the validator's ABI WARN reads 'the derived ABI record abstained (ABI_UNKNOWN): no reason recorded' even though inference T2 records the reason informally. An abstention with no machine-readable reason is the shape a reviewer least wants.
tooling_findings.not_fixed_here: Reported, not fixed. No tooling, validator or evidence file outside this VA's own package was modified.

tooling_findings.finding: RETURN SEMANTICS is NOT_AVAILABLE for this target because one of its two reachable returns is a call result, and that is the module's DOCUMENTED design rather than an accident: 'A CALL inside the body defeats this state on its own ... on x86-32 whether a caller may read EAX after a call is decided by the callee's signature, which this listing cannot show.' For a tail transfer the callee is not even named CALL in the listing but the transfer is treated the same way, so the state is UNCLASSIFIED and the check is NOT_AVAILABLE.
tooling_findings.evidence: Live verdict: 'the machine return state is UNCLASSIFIED and the source span declares return type SlotWord: the return register EAX is written at a width this module cannot bound on at least one of the 2 reachable return(s) in the complete 6-instruction listing (a call result, a conditional destination, or two returns reached with different widths), so no width is determinable.' The two reachable returns are 0x00c70e0f (`b8 01 00 00 00`, a boundable 32-bit immediate write) and the 0x00c70e0a transfer (unboundable).
tooling_findings.note: The module's route is not even entered here: `decide()` defers to the string-agreement arms whenever a canonical `return_type` claim exists, and the index projection deliberately files a worker's `observed_original_abi.return_type` under `return_note`, so no source-side declaration can change this verdict. Verified by adding `return_type` to this record's metadata and re-running: the verdict did not move.

tooling_findings.finding: AN INLINE-ASM BLOCK CONTAINING A CALL, WITH MEMORY OPERANDS, IS CODE-GENERATED WRONG: g++ held the -fPIC GOT base in EDX across the call and computed a POST-call operand address from it, while the callee uses EDX as its own scratch. In this package's ESP measurement the second sample was written through the clobbered base, the slot kept its initial value, and the failure read exactly like a reconstruction that had failed to balance its stack.
tooling_findings.evidence: Generated code for the failing spelling, verified by objdump at -O1: `__x86.get_pc_thunk.dx` -> `addl $0x5c29,%edx` (GOT base in EDX) -> `movl %esp,0x30(%edx)` -> `call *0x18(%esp)` -> `movl %esp,0x2c(%edx)`, against a callee whose body is `mov 0x13c(%ecx),%edx`. The recovered value was 0xf7805e7b where a stack address was expected. Adding an unrelated fprintf to the same function made the symptom vanish, which is what identified it as code generation rather than as a property of the reconstruction.
tooling_findings.mitigation_applied_here: Every thiscall trampoline in the model test now carries NO memory operand in any block containing a call, and pins the receiver to ECX ("+c"), the target to EDX ("+d") and the result to EAX ("=a"), so neither register allocation nor aliasing is possible; the ESP measurement was reduced to two single-instruction asm blocks around a plain C++ call. Codegen verified by disassembly at -O0, -O1 and -O2 for both compilers.
tooling_findings.why_it_is_worth_reporting: The promoted sibling package src/reconstruction/pkg_00b8dab0_field194_getter/ carries the SAME trampoline shape - one asm block that samples ESP, calls through a register and samples ESP again, with two `"=m"` operands straddling the call. Its build_matrix in the committed metadata records only g++ -O1 and -O2 with no -O0 and no clang++, and it was built before this pattern was found to be unreliable. It is a latent hazard in already-promoted work, not a defect in this package.
tooling_findings.not_fixed_here: Reported, not fixed. The sibling package belongs to another worker and was not touched.

tooling_findings.finding: _convention_key scans a free-text convention claim for the first of ("fastcall", "thiscall", "stdcall", "cdecl") that APPEARS ANYWHERE in it, in that fixed order and independently of position. A worker that writes an honest, detailed convention string which happens to DISCUSS the rejected alternative is therefore recorded as claiming the alternative, and the ABI arm then FAILs with 'source convention [thiscall] conflicts with persisted fastcall' - the opposite of the intent.
tooling_findings.evidence: Observed on this VA: the first metadata draft carried the full discrimination argument in `observed_original_abi.calling_convention` and mentioned __fastcall before __thiscall; the validator returned ABI = FAIL with detail 'source convention ['thiscall'] conflicts with persisted fastcall'. The claim reached the check through the index projection of the metadata, where `calling_convention` is passed through verbatim.
tooling_findings.mitigation_applied_here: The claim string is now short and names only __thiscall, exactly as the promoted sibling package's does, and the whole discrimination argument moved to a separate `calling_convention_discrimination` field where no tokenizer reads it. The result is ABI = WARN on the TF1 abstention rather than a false FAIL.

confidence: high for the mechanism (six instructions, one displacement, one branch whose rel8 equals the length of the jump it skips, one signed rel32 that computes to the recorded tail target, one bare RET), none for the field identities or for the meaning of either path's value
unresolved_questions: What does the word at receiver+0x13c name, and what class does the receiver belong to? Nothing in the pack names either; the receiver record is bounds_only and the types/globals/vtables categories are all MISSING.
Is the receiver argument a `this` or an ordinary first parameter? The bytes cannot say (see not_claimed), and the answer is what would settle __thiscall against __fastcall.
Is the constant 1 a boolean, an enum member, a sentinel, or a count? The four sampled callers only order the result against 0x4 and 0x5, which is consistent with every one of those readings.
Do the two paths' return values denote the same quantity? Nothing in the evidence settles it, and the two arms share one signature.

What class is the TAIL receiver, and does it need an AddRef? The tail target's body is seven bytes with no room for a reference call, so ownership is undetermined; the promoted sibling pkg-00b8dab0-field194-getter carries the same open question for the same word.

Why does the derived ABI record abstain with verdict ABI_UNKNOWN? Its own inference T2 gives the reason as the tail transfer - 'the function can reach a caller by transferring out of the listing, so the path that actually returns was never observed' - at confidence UNKNOWN. That observation is incomplete for this body: 0x00c70e0f/0x00c70e14 IS a returning path in the same listing, and the transfer's own target is a two-instruction body whose MOV EAX/RET was read live. See the tooling note in the report.

focused_test.assertion_style: abort on the first failure; each group names the hypothesis it refutes
coverage: A - the guard is on the LOADED WORD and its null arm returns exactly 1: a null word with a NON-NULL receiver yields 1, and yields none of the five trap tags, so a guard on the receiver (which would have taken the transfer arm) fails

B - the transferred object is the word at +0x13c and nothing else: four fully-formed 0x198-byte decoy receivers each with a DISTINCT word at their own +0x194 cover one-word-low, one-word-high, address-of-the-word and receiver-passthrough, and a four-case sweep proves the answer tracks the word at +0x13c rather than any cached object

C - 0x13c is a BYTE displacement: the disp32-as-element-count reading lands at byte 0x4f0, past the modelled extent; the header's named accessor and the entry's literal arithmetic are checked against each other; the tail's 0x194 is proved to belong to a strictly larger, distinct receiver
D - the body reads and never writes: the entire 0x688-byte arena is byte-identical before and after every call, on BOTH paths, and the canary bands on both sides are intact

E - the value crosses verbatim: nine extreme values and a 4x4 sweep of the byte pattern at +0x194 all come back unchanged, and four further distinct arena addresses all take the transfer. The note in the test states the honest bound: a word that is not a usable address cannot be exercised, because the faithful tail target faults on it exactly as the machine would

F - a wrong DISPATCH TARGET is observable and the trap is PROVEN LIVE, not assumed: the callable sentinel occupies the word immediately past the last modelled slot (asserted by offsetof), and the test actually calls the modelled slot, the sentinel and a decoy and requires three pairwise distinct return values, so a one-slot-too-far dispatch cannot land on a value that impersonates the right one

G - the ABI is MEASURED, not asserted: ESP is sampled immediately before the call and immediately after the return and must agree (the callee pops nothing), and a second receiver at a different address yields a different answer

H - the encoding IS the observed twenty-one bytes, byte for byte, with the ModRM fields decoded (mod=10, reg=ECX, rm=ECX on this body's load; mod=10, reg=EAX, rm=ECX on the tail's), and BOTH addresses are COMPUTED from the encoded operands - the rel32 to 0x00b8dab0 and the rel8 to 0x00c70e0f - so a wrong branch or jump displacement fails here rather than passing

I - the four sampled call sites' ordered comparisons against 0x4 and 0x5 behave as the binary's do, including that both paths can produce 1 and that they are distinguishable the moment the transferred word differs

mutation_tests.perturbation: write the transfer as a call plus an explicit return instead of a tail-shaped return
mutation_tests.observed: SURVIVES, and unkillable by construction at any level: `return f(x)` and `{ auto r = f(x); return r; }` are the same C++ program, and whether the compiler emits a jump or a call-plus-return is an EMITTED-CODE property that differs between -O0 and -O2 for the SAME source. Asserting it would mean asserting one compiler's register allocation. Recorded as a boundary, not papered over: the .cpp says in so many words that the transfer is written in the tail-shaped source form, that the compiler is free to emit either, and that the model test asserts the call and the receiver it was given - which is what the bytes pin - rather than pretending to assert the jump.
